Blocking merge on one remaining cross-platform parser issue found by independent review and reproduced locally. I cannot submit this as a formal request-changes review because GitHub says this account lacks explicit repository access.

On the current PR head `86b443550783c5eed4f4a21e708f52d9f8cd18be`, `ServerDirectory.parse()` rejects Windows-rooted hints on POSIX/WSL, but Windows-profile parsing still accepts POSIX-rooted hints and silently converts them into Windows paths. In `packages/server/src/server-directory.ts`, `parseWindows()` calls `normalize(raw)` without constraining the target profile, then `toWin32(...)` converts `/tmp/repo` to `\tmp\repo`. That means a request like `?directory=/tmp/repo` to a Windows OpenCode server is not rejected as foreign syntax and can route to a different directory than the client intended.

Local reproduction on the PR merge tree:

```text
/tmp/repo => \tmp\repo
file:///tmp/repo => ServerDirectoryParseError invalid
C:/Work/Repo => C:\Work\Repo
C:\Work\Repo => C:\Work\Repo
C:Work\Repo => ServerDirectoryParseError drive-relative
\\server\share\repo => \\server\share\repo
relative\repo => relative\repo
```

Required before merge:
- Reject POSIX-rooted paths in the Windows profile unless there is an explicit documented reason to treat them as native Windows current-drive paths.
- Add platform-independent unit coverage using `ServerDirectory.parse(input, { kind: "win32" })` for `/tmp/repo`, `file:///tmp/repo`, drive-root paths, drive-relative paths, UNC paths, and relative paths.

Honestly guys I would not expect native cursor support in opencode until cursor unwalls their garden and creates clearer integration path. Cursor has real value: models, auth, indexing, and composer etc, but the problem is that cursor will not hand that over in a format or shape opencode needs to stay in charge of tool use: read this file, write that file, ask for permission, continue after the result etc, cursor often wants to run its own agent flow instead. 

And importantly that's true even from my testing of their ACP re Jetbrains/Zed **and** cursor-agent. 

TL;DR blocker is mostly on cursor side, native support is worth exploring, but I wouldn't expect it anytime soon guys. 

The least worst option at this stage IMO is a bridge that, put simply, translates cursor talk into opencode talk and I'm not aware of what else does that then the above plugin (which now creates a hook in cursor-agent itself to steer models more effectively).

If you are interested I documented the current gates and blockers: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/opencode-cursor/blob/main/docs/architecture/cursor-acp-mcp-future.md

I strongly disagree with this and this is wy I believe this is the wrong direction.

The issue isn't the path — it's that `CLAUDE.md` can carry Claude-specific stuff OpenCode can't run: `@imports`, skills, hooks, slash-commands, whole orchestration layers like oh-my-claudecode. The more `CLAUDE.md` locations we follow, the more of that we drag in. I've already hit this: a global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` with an OMC block gets read by OpenCode, and it starts trying to call agents and commands that don't exist here. That's not graceful — it's just broken.

And it doesn't end. To follow `CLAUDE.md` *safely*, we'd have to learn every difference between the two tools — which instructions are portable and which are Claude-only — and keep chasing it as Claude Code changes. That's a compatibility tax with no ceiling.

`AGENTS.md` is the cross-tool standard; `CLAUDE.md` is Claude's. Let's lean on ours: extend `AGENTS.md` discovery (#11454), keep `CLAUDE.md` as a minimal fallback, and if someone wants their Claude setup, give them an explicit "import `CLAUDE.md` into `AGENTS.md`" — where they decide what carries over. Translate once, with the user in control. Don't sign up to follow another tool's instruction format forever.

Superseded — closing in favor of a cleaner, OGR-native approach.

Rather than a bespoke in-core classifier (+662 lines in `Permission.ask`), the command-approval gate is now a standalone OpenGuardrails (OGR) plugin that hooks the existing `tool.execute.before`, so it needs **no opencode core changes**:

- `openguardrails-instrumentation-opencode` (npm) — guards tool calls via the OGR `GuardEvent` → `Verdict` contract.
- `@openguardrails/core` (npm) — the reference runtime: deterministic text/regex rules and/or your own model as an LLM judge.

Agents configure their own guardrails in `.opencode/guardrails.json`. Source: https://github.com/openguardrails/openguardrails-js

Adding a data point: this same `NOT NULL constraint failed: session_message.seq` error **also reproduces via the headless `opencode run` path** (a different trigger than mid-session model switching), and it **still fails in `1.17.11`** — so it looks like the earlier headless-run fix (#31413 / #31412) regressed.

### Minimal repro (fresh session, no model switching)

```bash
opencode --version   # 1.17.11
opencode run -m opencode-go/glm-5.2 "Reply OK then stop"
```

### Actual result

Exits non-zero in ~1.6s with the generic client error:
```json
Error: { "name": "UnknownError", "data": { "message": "Unexpected server error. Check server logs for details." } }
```

The underlying cause shows in the server log:
```
ERROR service=server error=NOT NULL constraint failed: session_message.seq
  cause=SQLiteError: NOT NULL constraint failed: session_message.seq
  at SessionHttpApi.prompt
```

### Notes
- Reproduces with any model/provider (also hit it with the default model), so it's not glm-specific — it's the headless `run` → `SessionHttpApi.prompt` insert path failing to populate `seq`.
- Interactive (TUI) sessions on the same install work fine; only the headless `run` / programmatic prompt path triggers it.
- This makes `opencode run` unusable for automation/scheduled tasks (we hit it running unattended overnight; had to fall back to interactive-only capture).

### Workaround (for anyone blocked)
Avoid `opencode run` for automation; drive the model interactively, or use `opencode serve` + the HTTP API with an explicit `seq` if you control the payload. Confirming in case it helps narrow the fix — the `seq` population needs to cover the headless/programmatic prompt path, not just the TUI/switch paths.

Happy to provide fuller server logs or the `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` schema snapshot if useful.

+1 on a native `session.start` hook with a `source` matcher. Adding a data point from running the plugin workaround in production.

I ship a `session.created` plugin that auto-bootstraps session context (runs a setup script, surfaces a short status toast, injects a one-line primer for the model). It works well for fresh starts, and a couple of findings that might help scope this:

- **`session.created` fires on the first real interaction, not at TUI launch.** Bootstrapping on launch alone misses it; subscribing to `session.created` is the right trigger.
- **The factory can evaluate more than once per process** (e.g. a plugin present in more than one loaded config layer), so the handler can see `session.created` twice for one new session. A module-level `Set` of seen session ids keyed on `event.properties.info.id` dedupes it; without that guard, side-effecting bootstrap runs twice. A native hook with a documented at-most-once contract would remove this footgun.
- **The resume blind spot is the real gap, exactly as described above.** `--continue` / `--resume` / `/resume` produce no bus event, so a resumed session silently skips bootstrap and the context that startup loaded is absent for the rest of that session. There is no plugin-side workaround today -- `session.updated` is too noisy and carries no "this is a resume" signal. This is the one case the plugin pattern genuinely cannot cover.

For the matcher, the three sources in the proposal (`startup` / `resume` / `compact`) map cleanly onto how the lifecycle already behaves -- `compact` overlaps with the existing `session.compacted` event, and `startup` overlaps with `session.created`, so the net-new capability the native hook unlocks is really `resume`. Even just emitting a bus event on resume (without the full `session.start` hook) would close the gap for plugin authors.

Generic skeleton showing the `session.created` handler + the at-most-once dedupe guard: https://gist.github.com/cassiodias/83a56ad40e1add6b95ab9b7dc9d99963
